verdict.rationale: Anytype clearly stores all data locally in an encrypted 'Vault' that the user owns and the app works fully offline (anytype-docs-29, anytype-docs-44, anytype-docs-45), and it supports Markdown export/import so users can extract readable files (anytype-docs-11, anytype-docs-20). However, the primary on-disk store is a proprietary encrypted database, not plain files a user can read without the app — reading requires either the app or an explicit export step, and community reports note nuances around what is/isn't encrypted on disk (anytype-comm-8, anytype-comm-9), which is a secondary caveat not a full contradiction of local-first ownership. Missing for 10: native human-readable file format usable without the app (e.g., markdown-on-disk by default), and independent verification that exported data is a complete lossless mirror of the live store.
